Higher zeta derivatives do not readily inherit the method, whereas Dirichlet L-functions introduce a favorable conductor logarithm; after accounting for a possible zero at the origin, the remaining obstruction is compressed to estimating one origin logarithmic derivative as the conductor varies.

A log-conductor term assists the crucial inequality and may make it valid throughout the left half of the critical strip for sufficiently large conductor. If L(0)=0, the proposed normalization replaces L(s) by L(s)/s, and the problem is reduced to controlling L′(0)/L(0) as a function of the conductor parameter.
